title: Write the linear model from a word description
subtitle: Linear functions · 24 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **24 of the official questions in Linear functions are this one** — 10 Easy, 4 Medium, 10 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Easy tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- A real-world scenario describes a starting amount plus or minus a fixed amount per unit (per second, per year, per foot, per gallon).
- There is no table or graph, and all four answer choices are equations or functions built from the same numbers in different arrangements.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the starting value: the amount when the input is 0, which becomes the constant term.
- 2) Find the rate per single unit, dividing if the rate is given per several units, and give it the right sign.
- Adjust the input if the rate only starts after a threshold, such as (x − n).

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Mostly unhelpful for building the model itself.
You can check a choice by graphing it and testing one concrete case you can work out by hand, such as the value at input 0 or at input 1.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You swap the starting value and the rate, or use + when the quantity is decreasing.
The trap is also that you multiply by the 'per n units' figure instead of dividing, ignore a doubling or repetition, or forget that the per-unit charge only applies beyond an initial block.
